data.name: Exterior Cleaning in Victoria | What Melbourne Conditions Change | Prime Exteriors
data.description: Prime Exteriors works across metropolitan Melbourne. What the Victorian climate, the local water and the local building stock change about exterior cleaning, and the eighteen council areas with their own page.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time of year to have this done?

acceptedAnswer.text:
It depends entirely which job. Sealing wants summer, gutters want autumn, growth treatment works best in winter while the growth is active, and house washing peaks in spring because that is when a winter of green becomes obvious.

The one thing we would push back on is leaving gutters until spring. By then the autumn leaf has been sitting in water for three months and it has already done whatever it was going to do.

mainEntity.name: Why does the south side of my house always look worse?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Because it is the side that never properly dries. In the southern hemisphere a south facing wall gets the least direct sun, so after a Melbourne winter it holds moisture for weeks at a time and mould, algae and lichen take hold there first.

It is not a sign that side was built differently or cleaned badly. It is orientation, and it will come back on the same wall every few years no matter how well it is treated.

mainEntity.name: Do Victorian water rules affect the work?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Permanent water saving rules have applied in Victoria since the drought years, and higher restriction stages can limit washing of hard surfaces. We work to whatever is in force at the time.

In practice it rarely stops a job. Soft washing uses a fraction of the water a pressure clean does, and where a restriction does bite we will tell you before we book rather than on the day.

mainEntity.name: Does Melbourne water leave spots on the windows?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Less than most places. The mains supply here comes largely from closed catchments and is soft, so there is not much dissolved mineral to dry onto the glass in the first place.

Where spotting does show up it is usually sprinkler overspray, bore water or run off carrying something off a wall above, not the mains. That is a different problem and it is dealt with on hard water and mineral stain removal.

mainEntity.name: Is bluestone treated differently from concrete?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, and it is the most common mistake we are called in to undo. Bluestone is porous basalt. Acid wash lightens it permanently, high pressure opens the face, and both are irreversible on a hundred year old plinth.

It wants low pressure, neutral chemistry and, usually, a penetrating sealer afterwards so the next spill sits on top instead of going in.
